rule: A Ralph park citing `iteration ended without a pushed branch` may be loop infrastructure rather than the issue's work — check the claude-step outcome and the agent's own comment before believing the issue is stuck.
why: ops#44's two attempt-failures were claude-code-action rejecting bot-actor pushes, fixed in #119/#120; the issue was fine. Signal appeared independently on #39 and #240 too.

rule: Before re-queuing a previously blocked or parked issue, read its comment history — `closed_by_pull_requests` plus the current code is not sufficient evidence the blocker is gone.
why: ops#142 was re-queued by a 2026-09-14 burndown sweep that checked only closed PRs and code; it burned a full iteration rediscovering a blocker recorded in July. Adrian's own follow-up generalised the rule.

rule: When a gate fails citing a missing binary or dependency, install it and re-run before trusting that diagnosis — the real fault can be a stale config or an architectural mismatch underneath.
why: ops#178 parked blaming a missing Playwright Chromium binary; with Chromium installed the real faults were a stale DEFAULT_ROUTES list and a gate architecturally unable to test /ops/* (vite preview doesn't run the serverless gate API).

rule: A `ralph-gate` startup_failure with zero jobs run means caller/reusable permission or version skew on a stale branch — update the branch from `main` before concluding the shared engine regressed.
why: ops#144 root-caused the #133 outage: the engine's gate job began requesting actions:write, which a reusable can never exceed its caller's grant for; only pre-ops#132 branches lacked it.

rule: Before executing a deletion or cleanup issue, diff its stated premise against current `main` — a prior unrelated PR may have solved the problem differently, making the literal DoD stale. Stop and ask rather than deleting working code on the issue text's word.
why: ops#122's target dead code no longer existed as described; PR #124 had rescoped the suites a different way. The deletion was still wanted, but only a human could confirm that.

rule: Before tagging an issue ralph-ready, confirm the file or script it targets actually exists in this repo — stale board imports point at other repos.
why: ops#63 targeted scripts/check-typography-discipline.mjs, which has no history in ops; the stack trace pointed at the separate portfolio repo, already flagged do-not-re-file.

rule: Backlog items describing pre-extraction design-system structure (HDS pages, /hds routes) are suspect — ops consumes @hirobius/design-system and no longer authors or hosts it.
why: ops#70 wanted HDS doc pages absorbed into /ops/atlas; those pages had been moved out to the standalone design-system repo entirely.

rule: Before treating a `ralph-blocked: fix is in an open unmerged PR` as resolved, verify that PR's mergeable_state — a stale or conflicting branch stalls the whole queue under single-flight and must be closed and re-dispatched, not waited on.
why: ops#233's PR #235 went stale and conflicted with main after #244; a human closed it and re-dispatched, landing as #246.

rule: An issue whose DoD requires editing `.github/workflows/*` must be split before queueing: the workflow file goes to a human or an adr-eng PR, the rest is re-filed as a script/registry-only issue Ralph can push.
why: The bot's token lacks the workflows scope. ops#90, #240, #241 and #243 each independently did the full work and then died at the push — four issues rediscovering the same documented wall.

rule: A pre-commit gate must not hard-fail the hook on a warn-severity finding, and a pre-commit failure should be checked for reproducibility on `main` before being treated as this issue's fault.
why: ops#262: check-validator-wiring's substring matcher read a prose mention of 'audit-sbom' in a quality.yml comment as live wiring, emitting a warn-severity WIRING_DRIFT. run-gates.mjs/husky fail on any non-zero exit regardless of severity, so a false positive blocked every commit repo-wide.

rule: The harness park comment must echo the agent's own `ralph-blocked` reason rather than substituting a generic diagnosis — a mismatched park reason hides the true state from whoever reviews it.
why: ops#103's park said 'branch pushed but PR creation failed after 3 attempts (auth/network?)'. The agent had just correctly reported the issue was already shipped in merged PR #192 and no push had failed.

rule: A PR body's `Closes #N` is not proof the issue will auto-close — verify the transition after merge and close directly if it didn't, or the loop re-claims finished work indefinitely.
why: ops#156 accumulated 12+ ralph-blocked re-claims over ~12 hours on already-shipped work; ops#103, #3, #205, #210 and #282 show the same pattern.

rule: Treat a `ralph-blocked` comment that does not result in the issue actually being parked within one cycle as a harness defect to fix, not a reason to re-dispatch.
why: ops#156: 5+ blocked comments accumulated before parking stuck. The agent named the likely cause itself — reconcile_issue's blocked-parking path.

rule: GitHub's merge/compare APIs require a full 40-character SHA — a short SHA is rejected outright. Read it with `git rev-parse HEAD`, never `--short`, and never retype an abbreviated SHA copied from earlier push output. More generally: the SAME error twice in one session is a signal to change the procedure, not to retry it.
why: Rejected three times on 2026-09-16 while merging #332, #333 and #336 — identical error each time, because the short SHA was being lifted from 'git push' output. Harmless in itself (the API refuses rather than acting on the wrong ref) but it costs a round trip on every merge, and the repeat is the real finding: an agent that re-makes a mistake inside one session is not reading its own transcript.

rule: Before citing a stored field as evidence that something happened, find the code that WRITES it and the trigger that runs that code. A field that nothing can fill is not evidence of absence — it is a broken gauge.
why: `lastViolationAt` in docs/guardrails/registry.json reads as 'this gate has never caught anything', but it is structurally unfillable for two independent reasons: a pre-commit gate failure aborts the commit, so post-commit never runs; and the `&&` in .husky/post-commit:16 gates the bake on gate SUCCESS, so the one path that could write it only runs when there is nothing to record. Filed as ops#330.

rule: Unit tests over fixture HTML do not prove an extractor works. Run the real fetch path against ANY reachable live host before claiming it does — in a network-restricted container, check the proxy's noProxy list for one.
why: lib/leads/email-extract.mjs passed 28 fixture tests, then returned `npm-oidc-no-reply@github.com` on the first live fetch (registry.npmjs.org, reachable because it is in the proxy allowlist). JUNK_LOCALPARTS was an exact-match Set containing 'no-reply'; the localpart merely CONTAINED it, so every bounce-noreply@ and mailer-daemon@ had a free pass. One real sample found what 28 hand-written ones could not, because fixtures encode what the author already thought of.

rule: A closed issue is not proof its schema change reached the database. For any issue whose DoD includes a migration, verify the table/column exists in the live project before closing.
why: ops#78 is closed, but `digest_items` does not exist in vvyccwxtcwvlusweenje — and neither does `pitch_queue` (migration 0012). Repo migrations and the live ledger had diverged three separate ways with nothing gating that seam, while site-engine<->ops and site-engine<->snapshot both have gates. Filed as ops#348.

rule: A migration's FILENAME is a label for the change, not an inventory of the objects it creates. Read the SQL before asserting a migration did or did not run — and never infer 'unapplied' from the absence of a table named after the file.
why: ops#348 (p1, sev2, needs-adrian) concluded that 0012_pitch_queue.sql was never applied because no table named pitch_queue exists. No table by that name is created by any migration in the repo: 0012 creates lead_notes plus two leads columns, three indexes and RLS — all six objects verified present in vvyccwxtcwvlusweenje on 2026-09-16. The disproof was already inside the issue: its own query returned lead_notes and it was read as unrelated. The issue would have had a human run DDL on production on a half-wrong premise. Same family as 'find a stored field's writer before citing it as evidence' — here the artefact was a filename.

rule: Do not write a claim into always-on context (HANDOFF.md, status.json, CLAUDE.md) from memory. Re-verify it at the moment you write it. Always-on context is read and ACTED ON by every later session, so a wrong line there costs an iteration per reader, not per author.
why: On 2026-09-16 this session wrote '9 client-repo orphan branches, disjoint histories, content a subset of main' into ops status.json from recall of an earlier branch listing. Audited: there are 10, only 2 are unmerged, and one is a NET DELETION (index.html 1112 -> 541 lines on a live client page), not a subset. It happened one hour after this same session corrected another session for shipping a wrong migration warning into HANDOFF's Now section — so the failure is not rare, it is the default when a claim is cheap to state and nobody re-reads it before it lands. Corollary seen in the same audit: a branch's commit message is not evidence its work is unmerged; claude/autonomous-issue-handling-el4olq read as a 236-line unmerged feature but main already had it and had moved past it, so merging would have reverted work.

rule: lint-staged 17 disables file chunking when --max-arg-length is absent: it passes parseInt(undefined) = NaN. A commit staging ~140 files then spawns one prettier call longer than cmd.exe's command-line limit and the hook fails on Windows. Pass --max-arg-length explicitly.
why: A merge of main into an old branch staged ~140 files and the pre-commit hook died on Windows with no useful message. The hook had looked correct for months because a normal commit stages few enough files that one call fits. Fixed in ops#389 by pinning `pnpm exec lint-staged --max-arg-length 3000`. Generalises: a default that is silently NaN is worse than a missing default, because it disables a safety behaviour instead of erroring.

rule: A green merge button proves nothing when the only required check does not test the PR. Before merging, run the repo's real gate against the EXACT pushed head SHA — not the branch name, not a local working tree.
why: ralph-gate is ops's sole required check and it passes non-Ralph PRs untested, so an all-green PR page said only 'this is not a Ralph PR'. Merges on 2026-09-17 were only safe because the gate was run by hand on the pushed head. Branch protection that is satisfied by a check which opts out of testing is protection in name.

rule: An agent writing tests for a redaction or PII gate will reach for a real example, reintroducing the term the work exists to remove. Load the denylist before writing fixtures, and treat a passing gate with no denylist configured as 'unchecked', not 'clean'.
why: ops#386 shipped check-pii across pre-commit, commit-msg, PR/push and a weekly scan, but PII_DENYLIST and .pii-denylist are out-of-repo secrets that did not exist yet, so the gate matched only generic patterns. A client tenant's name landed in a PR test fixture on the same day and the gate passed it. The denylist is deliberately not in the repo (the list is itself PII), which means its absence is the default state, not an anomaly.

rule: Verify a plan-gated vendor capability against the vendor's own docs and pricing page BEFORE designing around it. A feature the CLI happily runs locally can still be unpublishable on the account's plan.
why: hds built Code Connect v2 templates generated from cva and gated them in CI (hds#214), then ADR-025 had to record that publishing custom Code Connect requires an Organization or Enterprise seat and the account is on Professional — `figma connect parse` runs locally on any plan, so nothing failed until publish. Same family as the REST variables API being Enterprise-only, which had already archived the previous sync workflow. The local tool working is not evidence the capability is available.

rule: A red-phase test that passes a path override the code does not read yet runs against the real default: give writers no reachable real default in tests, or assert the real file is unchanged.
why: While building ops#602, a test for persistLearnedRule({ filePath }) ran before the option existed and appended two stray rows to the real ledger; only the new ledger gate caught it.

rule: Never run `pnpm lint:fix` across the whole codebase; auto-fix one rule at a time and run typecheck plus the build after each pass.
why: In the Pod N incident a bulk ESLint auto-fix merged unrelated code blocks into syntax errors in three files and the work had to be discarded.

rule: Never auto-fix `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`; fix each dependency array by hand.
why: The auto-fix adds dependencies mechanically and introduces stale-closure bugs.

rule: Validate a change with the real build and the full test suite, not `pnpm typecheck` alone.
why: Typecheck configs cover only part of the tree and miss Vite-only import errors, so the Pod N breakage and a prop rename that missed test call sites both passed it.

rule: Dispatch any deletion task to sonnet or a stronger model, never haiku.
why: Deletions need judgement to find live consumers; in the Pod 2 near-miss haiku removed an export that still had three consumers.

rule: Before deleting a symbol or file, grep for live consumers and stop to report them if any exist.
why: A deletion with a live consumer breaks the build, and a single grep can still miss a consumer a prior PR left behind.

rule: Dispatch each sub-agent on the cheapest model that can do the job and state the model and effort choice in the dispatch.
why: Adrian set cost discipline as a standing directive: opus is the most expensive lever and most unit work does not need it.

rule: Cap concurrent agent pods at four or five, and lower on a small host.
why: More pods created merge hell, and four local pods risked running out of memory during gate spikes.

rule: Before a dispatched agent commits, verify its worktree isolation actually took (directory, branch and base).
why: The worktree flag was unreliable: pods wrote to main directly and one worktree was 258 commits behind, producing broken and cross-pollinated commits.

rule: When parallel agents could touch the same file, isolate them in worktrees and scope or sequence that file instead of letting them collide.
why: Parallel pods that all wrote one shared file produced collision commits that needed manual rescue.

rule: Ground every claim in an audit, report or commit message in a file line, command output or commit you actually checked.
why: An ungrounded doc audit ran about 55% false positives at P0, and later commits and ADRs asserted decisions and provenance the record did not support.

rule: Read the full gate error and fix its cause before retrying; never re-claim and retry a failing commit.
why: An agent re-claimed one unit 24 times while a single raw colour on an unrelated page blocked every commit.

rule: Run every CI check as a registered gate through run-gates, never as a bespoke workflow step.
why: One registry gives each check a firing channel and proof-of-firing fixtures, and a test stops the workflow from growing unregistered steps.

rule: Mark work done only when its own deliverable is in HEAD and its own check passes now.
why: Agents marked units done without shipping them because the done-check was a project-wide suite that passed regardless, and "I analyzed it" is not done.

rule: Push your `claude/*` branch with a draft PR early as your claim, and read live claims before touching a subsystem.
why: Two sessions collided three times in one day, and visible claims let a pre-flight catch duplicate work before it is built.

rule: Before numbering a new migration, check main and other open branches for that number.
why: Parallel sessions numbered 0012 twice and both reached the live database, and an earlier branch had to renumber 0004 to 0005.

rule: Stage files explicitly by path, never `git add -A`, in a tree other agents may share.
why: Another agent's work in progress in the same tree gets swept into your commit.

rule: Keep time-dependent checks (stale claims, review age) out of blocking pre-commit gates and report them as warnings or audits.
why: A runtime or timing condition is not a schema violation and must not lock every commit.

rule: Edit a generated file's source or generator and regenerate it; never hand-edit the output.
why: A hand edit to generated output is overwritten on the next run and hides drift between the source and the file.

rule: Give every generated file its generator in the repo and a `--check` that fails when the committed copy is stale.
why: A file labelled AUTO-GENERATED with no generator drifted six values, while every generated-and-checked surface in the ADR-010 audit was accurate.

rule: Keep unrelated churn (formatter rewrites, regenerated artifacts such as the SBOM) out of a PR and restore those files to main.
why: Base merges swept 36 unrelated files into one PR, and a sandbox SBOM regeneration produced a 111,574-line false diff.

rule: Fix a commit that broke the build with a new fix-up commit, never `--amend`.
why: Amending hides the breakage from the history and from anyone who already pulled it.

rule: Never raise a budget, regenerate a snapshot or weaken a test just to turn a gate green; find and fix what it reports.
why: A size budget raised as a workaround hid a solvable problem, and a drift snapshot regenerated on an unrelated PR would silence real drift between repos.

rule: Treat a new rule as unfinished until its gate is wired into a pipeline and proven to fire on a known violation.
why: The repo once had about 77 check scripts with only 8 running, and an inert safety apparatus defended a path nobody had walked.

rule: When a failure happens, add a check that catches it instead of a new paragraph of instructions.
why: Prose rules decayed: the session-end state duty, the run-log recap mandate and the board claim rule were skipped until a check or a derivation replaced them.

rule: Derive state (release, next, blocked, counts, claims) from git and live sources; never hand-write it into status files or steering docs.
why: The ADR-010 audit found every hand-written, unchecked state file wrong somewhere, while generated and checked files were accurate.

rule: Keep always-on agent context under an enforced byte budget and load everything else on demand.
why: Always-on context had grown to about 189 KB (47k tokens) and carried live contradictions such as a feature freeze that had been lifted.

rule: Make every failure (a gate, a token, a missing config) name what broke and the exact fix.
why: Generic errors and silent empty results left failures baffling, such as a token that labels fine but 404s on dispatch because it lacks Actions: write.

rule: Decompose an epic into sub-issues and ship the smallest well-scoped slice; never build or revive the umbrella wholesale.
why: Umbrella issues with no real DoD were structurally un-closeable, and the loop needs one deliverable per issue.

rule: When blocked on a human decision, drain the unblocked parts, then ask the specific question and stop rather than guess.
why: A clean blocked-stop routes the issue to a human without burning an attempt, while a guess costs rework or a wrong decision.

rule: Track work as GitHub Issues in the repo that owns it, never in a local TODO or backlog file.
why: Local backlogs went stale and could not sync to the ops hub, so BACKLOG.md was drained into issues and retired.

rule: Before filing or queuing an issue, check it is not already done: its closed_by_pull_requests, the code on main and its prior comments.
why: A 2026-09-14 sweep found 8 of 11 queued issues already shipped or obsolete, and a planned filing wave collapsed to zero new issues once checked.

rule: Queue an issue for an agent only when its DoD is a real `- [ ]` checklist that a separate process can verify mechanically.
why: Issues with no DoD, or a DoD of "accepted by Adrian", always parked and cost an iteration to discover.

rule: Give every open decision a default and a date (a Decision issue, or a tripwire with a pre-decided action) so silence resolves it.
why: Undated questions drift, while a default plus a date lets work proceed and keeps the human veto.

rule: Put work whose reason to act lies in the future in PARKED.md with a machine-checkable trigger instead of an open issue.
why: Open future reminders cost triage on every pass while never being actionable, and a parked entry keeps the detail until its trigger fires.

rule: When a parked item's trigger fires, file a fresh issue that cites the old one instead of reopening it.
why: A reopened issue carries a months-stale premise; one sweep found stale premises in six of the issues examined.

rule: File the concrete change as an issue, never an open-ended discussion with no deliverable.
why: A discussion issue cannot close; the frontier-engineering thread paid out only once its changes were filed separately.

rule: Never invent business facts such as phone, hours, reviews or names; leave an absent field absent or stubbed and list it as a TODO.
why: A fabricated detail on a client's live site is unrecoverable, which is why fabrication bans are an essential human gate.

rule: If a client request cannot be expressed in the ClientConfig schema, stop and flag it as a custom engagement; never add a per-client escape hatch.
why: The one-config-file contract is the factory's moat, and per-client markup dissolves the schema, the purity gate and fleet safety.

rule: Scaffold a client app with `pnpm new-client`, never by hand-copying files.
why: The script copies the canonical template and regenerates the generated app roster, which a hand copy skips.

rule: Do not modify `packages/*` or a shared `.astro` component while building a client; a shared change is a versioned fleet event.
why: A shared template change restyles every non-ejected site in the fleet.

rule: Validate client config at build time so an invalid config fails the build instead of shipping.
why: The Astro build runs defineClient's Zod validation, so a malformed site cannot ship by accident.

rule: Run the shared acceptance check on every client app so placeholder contact data, unbacked sections and an ungated production deploy fail the build.
why: Zod cannot catch placeholder URLs, stub phones or an open-by-default gate; the check caught a real unbacked section on its first run, and four deployed apps had been publicly reachable.

rule: Gate go-live on an armed acceptance build and a recorded shipping checklist.
why: `pnpm go-live` refusing without them keeps placeholder intake data from ever reaching production.

rule: Re-sync ops's vendored `lib/schema` in step with any change to site-engine's canonical `packages/schema`.
why: The two copies of the ClientConfig contract drift otherwise, and the drift guard then blocks unrelated PRs.

rule: Move code to its single home and freeze or delete the old copy; never keep a long-lived duplicate in two repos.
why: A duplicated token and governance pipeline drifted (18 of 196 copied files differed), so the engine moved to one repo and the old copy was frozen and then deleted.

rule: Pin every vendored copy (Ralph kit, skills, shared gates) by hash, check it locally at pre-commit and keep formatters off it.
why: Vendored copies drifted silently: Prettier rewrote pinned skills and shared scripts, and four apps kept an outdated copy of a shared preview gate.

rule: After renaming a GitHub org or repo, re-point Vercel git integrations and MCP repo scopes by hand.
why: GitHub redirects git remotes, but those integrations do not follow a rename automatically.

rule: Treat Vercel as folio's only deploy target; do not add Netlify files or assume a second deploy pipeline.
why: There is no other host, so second-pipeline configuration is dead weight that misleads the next reader.

rule: Pin Ralph callers to a version ref, never `@main`, and ship caller-breaking engine changes as a new tag re-pinned ops-first, never by moving or re-tagging the shared v1 branch.
why: Callers are vendored files that skew behind the engine; one engine change broke every gate run org-wide, and `git tag -f v1` would make `@v1` ambiguous for every consumer.

rule: Never reference a doc, path or workflow that does not exist; update docs to match the repo rather than its aspirations.
why: Steering docs pointed at files that were gone and at a DONE-LOG entry that never existed, so readers acted on structure that was not there.

rule: Define and query the fleet by its explicit allowlist of six repos, never by a list of names or by every repo the token can see.
why: Naming client repos in a doc leaked one, and an unscoped issues query counted 209 issues where the fleet had 95.

rule: Keep client and private-repo names out of anything public or shipped, including npm types, shipped docs and broadcast lists.
why: A consumer name shipped in published JSDoc types and a steering doc that listed client repos leaked private names.

rule: Do not expect an email from a Maps or Google Business Profile scrape; plan outreach on the phone unless a crawl finds an address.
why: Google Business Profile has no email field, so no Maps scraper returns one: of 39 qualified leads, one had an email and 38 had a phone.

rule: Do not raise dialling or "0 contacted" as a prompt or recommendation; answer only when asked.
why: Adrian's 2026-09-16 directive: the pressure to dial was pulling focus from the build.

rule: Aim the loop at the North Star path before building more machinery; merged cleanup volume is not progress.
why: On 2026-09-14 the loop merged 15 dead-code PRs while the p0 that makes money sat 64 days unqueued, and twenty PRs of scaffolding left the funnel unchanged.

rule: Label a qualifying issue `ralph-ready` in the same action that files it, and state a reason on the issue when you leave it unqueued.
why: The best-specified p0 sat 64 days because nobody applied one label.

rule: Keep three to five `ralph-ready` issues in the pool, fed in small batches, and leave it non-empty at session end.
why: An empty pool idles the loop because a park never re-triggers it, and mass-tagging churns issues into parks.

rule: When the loop parks an issue for a missing DoD, draft the checklist as a comment for a thumbs-up instead of bouncing it back.
why: A park for a missing DoD is a context gap, not a rejection, and a comment never overwrites what a human wrote.

rule: Write one spec file with rejected alternatives for an epic (more than three issues, or client output, PII or money), and none for a chore.
why: The rejected-alternatives step is the one historically skipped, and a spec for a one-file fix is pure overhead.

rule: Give every editorial doc an owner, a review date and a maximum age that a check reports.
why: Documents here outlive their truth: HANDOFF reached 119 KB against its one-page contract and old specs kept reading as live.

rule: Trigger lesson capture on failure events (parks, gate failures, reverts), not on task completion.
why: Hermes distilled task trivia because it ran its post-mortem on completion, while the loop's own failure comments held the real lessons unread.

rule: Attach every capture step to an event that is always written (a park, a merge, a gate failure), never to a process or to someone remembering.
why: Four capture loops (learned-rules, agent-heal-log, run-log and the decision ledger) died silently when their process or the habit went away.

rule: Ship every capture pipeline and scheduled loop with a liveness check that fails when it produced nothing while its source events occurred.
why: An empty log and a healthy-but-idle one look identical, and site-engine's loop ran without a watchdog for two months unnoticed.

rule: Surface counts, truncation and failures where a human already looks (the page, the PR), never only in a log or console.
why: A truncated fleet read was reported only to console.warn, which nobody reads on a serverless function, so the page under-reported silently.

rule: Keep human gates on irreversible actions (client PII, fabrication, money, outbound sends, secrets, history rewrites) however good agent context gets.
why: Their failure modes are unrecoverable: a fabricated detail on a live client site, a real send, a leaked key.

rule: Replace an approval label that is always applied with a path rule in code.
why: A label you always apply is approval theatre, and leaving the revenue boundary to a label or to model judgement let supervised diffs merge unreviewed.

rule: Tag `ralph-auto` only on an issue whose DoD names no supervised path.
why: Blanket ralph-auto let two lead-handling diffs merge unreviewed while the engine had no path check.

rule: Split a catch-all human-gate label into real decisions and credential chores.
why: Most human-gated issues sat under one catch-all label, many already dispositioned, which hid the few that needed Adrian.

rule: In ops, prefer deleting an unused surface to preserving it and keep only end-to-end and invariant tests; treat client-facing repos the opposite way.
why: ops is an internal dashboard an agent can rebuild in an afternoon, while client-facing repos touch PII, money and visible output.

rule: Measure direction (North Star share, human-gate latency), never commit, PR or line counts.
why: Volume metrics would have scored superbly on the day the loop shipped nothing that earns.

rule: Keep one document per subject and replace a stale one rather than adding another.
why: This fleet rots documents: two ADR registries diverged, and a three-file spec triad was collapsed because one file is one thing to keep true.

rule: Record a reversal or override of a decision as a new dated entry instead of silently rewriting or skipping it.
why: A recorded reversal keeps the trail trustworthy, and because Accepted ADRs are immutable a correction is a new ADR.

rule: Do not reopen a recorded decision without new evidence that its premise changed.
why: Settled decisions kept being re-proposed on surface similarity, and reversing load-bearing ones would regress working code.

rule: Run `pnpm typecheck:api` after touching `api/`; Vercel type-checks serverless functions and `vite build` does not.
why: A branch error-deployed for seven commits because a green local build hid missing function types.

rule: Give every relative import in `api/*.ts` an explicit `.mjs` or `.js` extension.
why: The deploy is ESM, so an extensionless import type-checks green and then 500s with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND; the whole /ops board hung on it.

rule: Set Vercel env vars for both Production and Preview, then push a new feature-branch build to apply them.
why: A Production-only var is invisible to previews, and the dashboard Redeploy re-runs stale main instead of the branch.

rule: Never write to the repo tree from a Vercel function; only /tmp is writable.
why: An append to a committed JSONL file would throw EROFS in the real Lambda.

rule: Never put a secret in a `VITE_` variable or verify auth in the browser; move the check server-side.
why: Vite inlined a portal HMAC secret into the static bundle, so anyone could read it and mint a token.

rule: Keep each client's work repo private and Hirobius-owned, and hand the client a curated deliverable, never the repo.
why: Client PII and internal business content live safely in the work repo only because it is private.

rule: Bootstrap every fresh clone or worktree (install plus generators) before running hooks or verification.
why: Fresh worktrees lack node_modules and gitignored generated files, so pre-push died with ENOENT after minutes of other gates.

rule: Keep hooks fast and quiet, printing a short failure summary and a log path.
why: An eight-minute opaque pre-push made agents grep logs by hand and rerun the whole chain for each failure.

rule: Give agents the access to verify their own work (preview bypass, live tokens, browsers) and check it at session start.
why: Previews behind SSO, 403 tokens and blocked browser downloads left fixes unverified across many sessions.

rule: Use `set -o pipefail`, or no pipe, when piping a command whose exit code matters.
why: `git push | tail` hid three failed pushes.

rule: Read `git diff --stat` before dumping a large diff into context.
why: 40 KB diffs were dumped into context when the stat would have scoped the read.

rule: Keep every shared list (labels, fleet repos, routes, nav entries) in one constant that everything imports, with a test.
why: Parallel copies drifted: a label split missed BLOCKING_LABELS, four nav lists diverged, a hardcoded FLEET_REPOS saw three of six repos and a stale route allowlist masked a dead link.

rule: Fix, reclassify or remove any gate or warning that fires for reasons unrelated to the change.
why: Irrelevant failures and constant warnings trained agents to ignore warnings and bypass hooks with --no-verify, which also skipped the gates that matter.

rule: Message Adrian only when done, blocked or needing a decision, in five lines or fewer with no narration.
why: Long reports kept arriving despite the rule and spend Adrian's attention, the loop's scarcest resource.

rule: Hand off between sessions with a direct message or doorbell trigger, not a file or Adrian's copy-paste.
why: A file nobody is told to read is never read, and relaying by hand kept Adrian in the loop.

rule: Give Adrian paste-ready text and a deep link to the exact place for every field or file he has to fill by hand.
why: Directions and pasted YAML turned human steps into slow phone copy-paste jobs.

rule: Skip builds for docs-only diffs but always build a diff you cannot classify.
why: Build minutes were about half a Vercel invoice, and defaulting unknown diffs to a build keeps the skip safe.

rule: Treat "could not check" as its own failing state, never as the expected signal: fail closed and say so.
why: A red-first check in a bare worktree read every test as red and passed, an unreachable URL read as dead, and a fail-open fallback re-selected issues that should have parked.

rule: Verify a scheduled Routine's first run did real work, and prefer a GitHub Action for jobs that need repo access.
why: Routines created without repos or connectors 403 on clone and API calls, while an Action's job token always works.

rule: Verify accessible names and rendered output in the rendered DOM, not by reading the source props.
why: The HDS Button documented a label prop it never emitted, so every control announced only its text, and only the rendered DOM showed it.

rule: When extracting a business email, prefer a mailto on the business's own domain.
why: Trade-site footers routinely carry the web designer's address.

rule: Fix or delete a permanently red test instead of tolerating an expected red.
why: Eight months-red Playwright specs kept main red and masked real failures until they were removed.

rule: Count rows with COUNT(*), never a pg_stat estimate.
why: A stale pg_stat estimate read 0 for a table that held 263 leads.

rule: Prove a stage with a live state that a failure cannot satisfy, not a stored string or flag.
why: A stage counted any stored preview URL, which a 404 satisfies, and a stored qualified flag drifts whenever the scorer is reweighted.

rule: In a squash-merge repo, treat a merged branch as dead (restart it from origin/main) and judge merged-ness by tip SHA against the merged PR head, never by git ancestry.
why: Ancestry matched 0 of 164 merged branches, a diff-based check fired on 101 of 102, and a stop hook advised pushes that would have built forks.

rule: Check that a branch contains main with `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD`, not the reverse.
why: The obvious check, `--is-ancestor HEAD origin/main`, is false for every healthy in-progress branch.

rule: Land or unblock open PRs before building new work, and never rebuild a PR that is waiting on a human.
why: A night that started with four open PRs and no merges ended with eleven merged once landing came first, and rebuilding a waiting PR duplicates work.

rule: Cite an ADR by its full path, never by a bare number.
why: Two unrelated records both read as "ADR 2", and a theming comment cited the wrong ADR number for months.

rule: Verify through the API that a merge completed before treating it as merged.
why: A merge tap that did not complete left the loop idle for four hours.

rule: When the Ralph queue stalls, check open `ralph/*` PRs before the run history, because one unmergeable or unapproved PR halts single-flight.
why: Run history cannot tell "nothing to do" from "blocked on one PR" since both are fast green no-ops, and a five-hour wedge hid behind a healthy-looking queue.

rule: Exit non-zero on an unknown CLI flag instead of printing help and exiting 0.
why: A logging script treated a wrong flag as a help request, so callers with bad syntax were told they had succeeded.

rule: Rebase or re-implement before reusing an old branch, because its diff against main shows main's newer work as deletions.
why: A stale draft branch showed a whole shipped feature being deleted, an artifact of branch age rather than intent.

rule: Let deterministic code choose the loop's next task (priority label, then issue number), never the model.
why: A deterministic selector parks malformed or capped issues with a written reason instead of working them blindly or retrying forever.

rule: Claim loop work with an atomic git ref create so two runners can never win the same issue.
why: Creating a ref is a true test-and-set, and claim comments keep ownership visible.

rule: Give a loop runner a documented exit-code contract that its driver acts on.
why: Distinct exit codes for shipped, empty, concurrent, parked, blocked and error replaced silent hangs and deaths.

rule: Build logic as a pure core with injected I/O (fetch, clock, client) behind a thin shell.
why: A pure core tests every edge case with no network, scratch repo or fake timers, and keeps resumed runs deterministic.

rule: Apply a migration to the live database before recording it in the migration ledger.
why: Recording first asserts a table that does not exist, which is how the repo and the live database diverged.

rule: Read each repo's default branch from the API, never assume `main`.
why: Two of the six fleet repos did not use main, which produced false positives in an audit and made Closes #N silently no-op.

rule: Open at least a draft PR for every pushed branch that did work, because a branch with no PR is invisible.
why: 86 fleet branches never had a PR and were invisible to the boards, the watchdog and gh pr list, which stranded one fix for two months.

rule: Clear `GIT_*` environment variables in test setup before tests run git.
why: Tests that run git under a worktree's pre-push hook inherit GIT_DIR and can commit into the real repo.

rule: Never retire or flip a working mechanism until its replacement is built and running.
why: Moving the watchdog to a local runner that was never built caused a two-month hds outage, and flipping the auto-merge default before the engine path check would delete the revenue boundary.

rule: Before building any issue, verify its stated premise against main and the live system.
why: Issue text goes stale: one sweep found stale premises in six issues, and several issues cited fixes or root causes that never held on main.

rule: Check that a test exercises the surface it names, because a suite that renders the wrong screen passes while testing nothing.
why: About 86 visual baselines and every a11y case audited one identical login-gate screen, and layout checks stayed silently empty without a main landmark.

rule: Follow Link-header pagination on GitHub list APIs and report any truncation.
why: A single-page issues fetch silently dropped issues once the fleet passed 100 open.

rule: Run Playwright suites that share a local server port one at a time.
why: Parallel suites on one port broke the first accessibility hard-stop pass.

rule: In cloud containers, link the shipped Chromium revision to the one Playwright expects instead of treating missing browsers as a code failure.
why: The container ships r1194 while the pinned Playwright wants r1208, so layout tests failed 15 of 15 for environment reasons.

rule: Let unattended automation take only mechanical actions (merge, abandon, re-dispatch) and report anything that needs a fix.
why: A watchdog that fixes red CI unattended is how a test gets skipped at 3am.

rule: Keep `@deprecated` JSDoc text on one line.
why: The manifest generator drops only @-leading lines, so a multi-line tag leaks into the component description.

rule: Render embedded legacy HTML reports in an iframe sandboxed without same-origin.
why: Without same-origin a report's scripts cannot reach the ops session cookie.

rule: Decide by measurement (a live run, a survey of real systems) rather than by a theoretical ranking or formula.
why: Fencing ranked first in theory and worst in a live lead pull, and a survey of real design systems overturned a ratio-based type scale.

rule: Check that every lead segment can reach the qualifying threshold, and weight a business with an existing DIY site as a proven buyer.
why: A 59-point ceiling against a 60 threshold made custom-domain leads unqualifiable while the weights ranked the hardest sells highest.

rule: Record outcomes in a closed vocabulary, not free text.
why: 200 calls logged as free text are anecdotes, not data.

rule: Do not record calls to Washington leads without all-party consent.
why: Washington, where most of the call list sits, requires all-party consent to record.

rule: Store notes as rows in a table, never as a column.
why: A column keeps only the latest note and loses the conversation.

rule: Keep scripts and hooks Windows-safe and test their path handling on a Windows checkout.
why: Two Windows path bugs failed the pre-push suite on every Windows checkout.

rule: Gate every `var(--…)` reference against the generated token set.
why: References to non-existent custom properties fail silently: camelCase typography vars and a missing spacing step resolved to nothing.

rule: Give every temporary construct (a deprecation, a feature flag) a dated removal step enforced by a check.
why: Open-ended @deprecated tags and flags never get removed and become permanent dead branches.

rule: Verify an architecture review's unify-the-duplicates recommendation against the code before building the shared abstraction.
why: Four similar state machines differed on axes a shared hook would have to absorb, so it would have been an over-parameterised shallow module.

rule: Scope a library's element and global styles under a root attribute instead of shipping global resets.
why: Global body fonts and resets fought an external consumer's own baseline and broke its page.

rule: Gate a large deletion on a check of the invariant it must preserve, and cut it one revertible PR at a time.
why: Deletion PRs gated by a consumer smoke test proved the published surface never changed.

rule: Remove gates and meta-audits that grade the system's own housekeeping rather than the product.
why: A strength scoreboard and auto-written health logs created churn while measuring only the discipline itself.

rule: Build a component for a measured consumer need, not to close a coverage-benchmark gap.
why: A date-picker family shipped for a benchmark with two runtime dependencies, and no consumer ever imported it.

rule: Ship frequently changing data separately from the code that reads it.
why: Baking the token model into the Figma plugin meant almost every plugin copy carried data, not code.

rule: Unescape HTML entities before comparing use_figma reads with committed values.
why: A variable description read through use_figma comes back HTML-escaped while writes store it raw, so a naive read never matches.

rule: Batch Figma MCP calls within the plan's daily budget and never retry a rate-limit error.
why: Retries burn the 200-call daily budget the Pro plan allows.

rule: Build roadmap, status and process UI from bands, dividers, rails and disclosures, not repeated outlined cards.
why: Outlined-card overload shipped repeatedly while the rule lived only in prose.

rule: Put status in a consistent metadata slot, rail, header zone or table column, never as a badge appended to prose.
why: Status scattered through prose as decoration cannot be scanned in one place.

rule: Settle each UI need with one named component and list the wrong answers agents reached for instead.
why: Two agents given the same screen should build it the same way, and naming the usual wrong pick stops the repeat.

rule: Pair a text token only with the surface it was designed for, and gate contrast for every preset and override.
why: A hero paired on-primary text with the fg surface and one preset rendered at 1.07:1, while the others looked fine only by accident.

rule: Run Lighthouse and axe with reduced motion forced.
why: They never scroll, so mid-fade sections read as false contrast violations and sent agents chasing speculative fixes.

rule: Ship motion with a reduced-motion guard and content visible by default, never hidden until JavaScript runs.
why: A prototype hid content behind opacity 0, so a visitor without JavaScript saw a blank page.

rule: Add visual variety as whole skins over a fixed page structure, not as more per-section variants.
why: Each variant adds permanent maintenance for less perceived difference, while three skins over one structure read as genuinely different sites.

rule: Keep folio's motion on the compositor (CSS reveals and fades, an absolute canvas) with no per-frame scroll JavaScript.
why: Per-frame scroll JavaScript reintroduces jank, and main-thread contention starved the text cascade until GSAP was removed.

rule: Render the WebGL scene on demand, capped at the device tier fps and paused offscreen.
why: The transmission pass re-renders the scene every frame and is too costly at full refresh.

rule: Scale only fidelity across GPU tiers, keep the same glass look, and give no-GPU devices a static image.
why: Mobile is not a downgrade signal, and a downgrade-only adaptive step catches weak GPUs without oscillating.

rule: Check WebGL changes on a real GPU before deleting a scene input that looks unused.
why: The env map looked unused at intensity 0 but feeds the transmission glass; the sandbox's software renderer could not show it, so it was deleted and had to be restored.

rule: Stash an agent's uncommitted or unshipped work on reset; never destroy it.
why: Salvaged work can be recovered after a failed attempt, while a hard reset loses it.

rule: Before pushing a `ralph/issue-<n>` branch, check for a stale same-named remote branch from a closed PR and confirm no open PR uses it.
why: Leftover branches from closed PRs rejected the push and invited force-pushes over refs nobody had checked.

rule: Do not make every branch edit one shared state file; write a per-branch note folded on main, or derive the value.
why: status.json, SESSION-BOARD and HANDOFF conflicted on almost every merge and pushed agents into hand edits to pass freshness checks.

rule: Fix a measurement baseline window with no system changes landing inside it.
why: Changing enforcement mid-measurement changes outcomes and corrupts the comparison.

rule: Put a plan through a fresh-context adversarial review before executing it.
why: An adversarial review of the factory plan found 13 issues, several of which changed the plan.

rule: Route engineering skills as mandatory steps enforced by a hook, not as optional suggestions.
why: Skills only earn their keep when invoked deterministically; an optional step gets skipped.

rule: Give each session its own `claude/*` branch and never put two sessions on one branch.
why: Branch-per-session is part of the collision-safety policy adopted after parallel sessions collided.
